{
  "candidate_rtl": "module ticket_machine #(
    parameter ON  = 1'b1,
    parameter OFF = 1'b0
) (
    input  clk, clear, ten, twenty,
    output reg ready, dispense, return_sig, bill
);

    reg s_ready, s_disp, s_return;
    reg s_bill10, s_bill20, s_bill30;
    reg bill_active;

    wire take_twenty = twenty & ~ten;
    wire no_payment = ~(ten | twenty);
    wire any_payment = ten | twenty;

    wire next_ready = s_disp | s_return | (s_ready & no_payment);
    wire next_bill10 = (s_ready & ten) | (s_bill10 & no_payment);
    wire next_bill20 = (s_ready & take_twenty)
                    | (s_bill10 & ten)
                    | (s_bill20 & no_payment);
    wire next_bill30 = (s_bill10 & take_twenty)
                    | (s_bill20 & ten)
                    | (s_bill30 & no_payment);
    wire next_disp = (s_bill20 & take_twenty) | (s_bill30 & ten);
    wire next_return = s_bill30 & take_twenty;

    // Union of the three next billing states, factored independently
    // of their individual next-state equations.
    wire next_bill_active = (s_ready & any_payment)
                          | s_bill10
                          | (s_bill20 & (ten | ~twenty))
                          | (s_bill30 & no_payment);

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (clear) begin
            s_ready     <= 1'b1;
            s_disp      <= 1'b0;
            s_return    <= 1'b0;
            s_bill10    <= 1'b0;
            s_bill20    <= 1'b0;
            s_bill30    <= 1'b0;
            bill_active <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            s_ready     <= next_ready;
            s_disp      <= next_disp;
            s_return    <= next_return;
            s_bill10    <= next_bill10;
            s_bill20    <= next_bill20;
            s_bill30    <= next_bill30;
            bill_active <= next_bill_active;
        end
    end

    always @* begin
        ready      = s_ready     ? ON : OFF;
        dispense   = s_disp      ? ON : OFF;
        return_sig = s_return    ? ON : OFF;
        bill       = bill_active ? ON : OFF;
    end

endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The measured baseline critical path is a state-register Q through a three-input OR to bill, with 0.70 ns arrival and 9.30 ns slack. Register-to-register paths already compete at 9.38 ns and 9.40 ns slack.",
  "rewrite": "Express the six reachable one-hot state transitions directly and add a synchronously updated billing-status register. Compute billing status from the current state and payment inputs for the upcoming state, rather than registering the current bill output. This removes the billing-state OR from the output path without adding an output cycle. Factor the billing-status D equation independently to avoid simply cascading the individual next-state equations into another OR.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Unmeasured candidate: for default parameters, bill becomes a direct register output. The added bill_active D cone, including synchronous clear, is a significant competing path and may eliminate the benefit or regress WNS. Existing state-transition paths can also become critical. If only the original output path were removed and every other path stayed unchanged, the supplied baseline gives a 9.38 ns WNS ceiling, or 0.08 ns improvement. Actual WNS improvement and non-regressing TNS require EDA confirmation.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Expected mapped register count is seven rather than six, subject to synthesis optimization. One additional dfxtp_1 costs 20.0192 um2, leaving only 5.25504 um2 of the original incremental budget before combinational changes. Removing the bill output OR recovers some area, while the new billing-status D logic and possible buffering consume area. The direct transition equations may also change mapping. Compliance with the 278.01664 um2 cap is not established and must be checked after mapping.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Retains the module name, parameter declarations and defaults, ports, synchronous active-high clear, and single positive-edge clock. After the specified startup reset, the six state bits remain one-hot and bill_active equals the union of the three billing states. All transitions preserve ten priority when both payment inputs are high. Arbitrary later clear assertions restore ready and clear billing status at the same edge as the reference. Outputs retain the reference cycle latency. No initialization, assertions, assumptions, additional startup cycles, or helper modules are introduced. Illegal internal encodings before the specified reset are not claimed equivalent; formal equivalence must use exactly the original fixed startup contract."
}
